stories.author: The Lever team
stories.title: Airlines Are Lobbying To Change Airfare Font Sizes. It's Gonna Cost You.
stories.text: For decades, buying a plane ticket hasn’t been a simple process. In the late 2000s, consumers were inundated with ads for special $79 or $99 flights, but were met with sticker shock when they went to buy the tickets and saw the true cost was actually much higher. Regulators, recognizing the headache this bait-and-switch created for consumers, established regulations requiring airlines to prominently display the total ticket cost at checkout. Today, buying a plane ticket still isn’t exactly easy: Consumers have to wade through a web of car and hotel bundles, seat upgrades, and baggage fees, but at least when they reach the checkout page, they can see the total cost of their flight prominently displayed in a larger font size than other charges, such as taxes and fees. But that may soon change, after airlines and industry groups have spent tens of millions lobbying Congress, the White House, and other regulators, and donated tens of thousands of dollars to Republican members of Congress. stories.text: Rep. Kaela Berg, Sen. Four super PACs with ties to AIPAC and Democratic Majority for Israel have surged into a Minnesota House race in the final months of the campaign, hoping to fend off the latest progressive insurgent. In the three-way race, one candidate, Matt Klein, is unapologetically supportive of Israel, while two others, Matt Little and Kaela Berg, have been critics to varying degrees. Little, however, has the support of the group A New Policy, which was founded to support pro-Palestinian candidates and lobby Congress against Israeli interests. Another PAC, called American Priorities, which was organized to be a counterweight to AIPAC, has jumped into the race to support Little with a spend of some $60,000. 314 Action, a super PAC ostensibly organized to support scientists and medical professionals, this week reported spending nearly $2.5 million supporting Klein, a staggering amount in a previously sleepy race, given that the PAC has raised just $15 million for the full cycle. stories.author: Judd Legum
stories.title: PopInfo Weekly: Fakes, falsehoods, and favors
stories.text: Last week, Popular Information reported that a New York Post headline falsely claimed that “Thousands of 9/11 families demand Mamdani be banned from 25th-Anniversary.” But a Popular Information interview with the organizer of the petition revealed that this was false, and that there was not an actual list of family members who signed the petition. The media outlets that pushed the false narrative later tried to cover their tracks. One of the outlets that published the New York Post’s false narrative was CBS News New York. But this week, CBS News New York aired a new segment highlighting people with family members who died on 9/11 “defending Mayor Mamdani’s inclusion in this year’s solemn remembrance ceremony.” One Nation, an opaque nonprofit affiliated with Senate Republicans, spent $1.7 million in less than a week on a new ad attacking Senator Jon Ossoff (D). The ad received 78 million impressions across Georgia. But almost nothing in it is true. The ad attacks Ossoff for positions that have actually been pursued by Republicans, including cutting the child tax credit.
